details:
Our project is basically an online museum website. It puts together 11 machines, landers, and rovers that NASA left on the Moon and Mars. When you open the site, you can pick either the Moon or Mars to start looking around. If you click on any machine, like the Apollo 11 tools, Lunar Roving Vehicles, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, or Insight, you get to read its story, some mission facts, and what it found in space. We also built a timeline on the site that covers big steps in space travel from 1969 up to 2022.

We did this project because we wanted space history to feel fun and easy to understand for anybody using a normal web browser. You don't need fancy equipment or any background in space science to use it. We really hope students, teachers, and people who just enjoy looking at the stars find it inspiring. Our main goal is to help keep human space history alive and let people know about the stuff NASA left out there. We also made sure to show the difference between tools left behind on purpose, experiments that were turned off, and spacecraft that simply reached the end of their work.

For the coding part, our team used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. We double-checked all the dates and science info from NASA’s real records to make sure we didn't get anything wrong. What makes our site a bit different is how we tell the story. We used the idea of a "museum without walls" to bring real history and science facts together.

While building everything, we tried hard to keep the history and science accurate. We also wanted to be fair to visitors, so we clearly separated actual NASA data from our own creative quotes. On top of that, we worked on making the design fit different screen sizes and keeping it super easy to click around the pages.
